desc: Parse input: N and the N×N character grid; build for each letter c a list of directed edges (u, v) with that label, plus an adjacency structure: for each vertex v and letter c, list of predecessors u with edge u->v labeled c.
Initialize dist array of size N×N with infinity; set dist[x][x] = 0 for all x; set dist[u][v] = 1 for every existing edge u->v (min over labels).

Implement Dijkstra over pair-states: from state (u, v) with distance d, for each letter c, for each edge u->u' labeled c and each edge v'->v labeled c, relax (u', v') with d+2. Use a heap; skip stale entries.
Optimize transition enumeration: precompute out-by-label[u][c] = list of u', and in-by-label[v][c] = list of v'; iterate only over non-empty label groups (product of list sizes).
After Dijkstra, build output matrix: A[i][j] = dist[i][j] if finite else -1; print N rows of space-separated values.
Verify logic against the samples mentally (e.g., (1,4) = 4 via abba) and check edge cases: N=1, self-loops, unreachable pairs.
Write the complete Python solution implementing the pair-state Dijkstra with in/out-by-label tables and early-break optimization, reading stdin and writing the answer matrix to stdout.
